title: quantization-performance-quality-benchmarks-int8-fp8-gptq-awq-kernels-2026-02-15
content:
Executive summary:

This doc summarizes the latest end-to-end and kernel-level benchmarks comparing INT8 (symmetric/affine), FP8 (E4M3-like), GPTQ, and AWQ quantization strategies on representative LLMs (7B and 13B variants) with our serving runtime kernels. The aim is to quantify the latency/throughput gains and the corresponding quality regressions (perplexity and LAMBADA/zero-shot QA proxies) and to call out kernel-level bottlenecks and optimization opportunities.

High-level conclusions (short):
- INT8 (well-calibrated per-channel affine) gives the best latency/throughput win on current kernels (avg ~1.8-2.5x token/sec improvement vs fp16) with small quality drop for 7B and acceptable drop for 13B after activation rescaling.
- GPTQ and AWQ provide superior quality retention vs naive INT8 for many workloads; latency is similar to INT8 in our optimized kernels but requires additional dequant path cost in some layers (p99 +5-10% compared to INT8).
- FP8 yields modest compute reductions but is currently limited by lack of fused kernels and numeric instability on a few ops; throughput win ~1.2x over fp16, quality close to fp16 for 7B, slightly worse for 13B without per-layer tuning.
- Kernel hotspots remain GEMM (matmul), softmax/QKV attention kernels, and KV cache memory copies. Our fused matmul+dequant and fused qat kernels show largest wins.

Experiment setup:
- Models: Llama-2-7B-chat, Llama-2-13B-chat (weights converted to our internal format).
- Workloads: synthetic token-by-token streaming prompt (avg prompt len 64), batched completion workloads (batch sizes 1,4,8), generation lengths 64 and 256.
- Hardware: 1xA100-80GB (pinned), 1xH100-80GB for FP8 cross-checks.
- Runtime: redwood-runtime v0.42.1 with kernel flags: --kernels=fused-matmul-dequant, --kv-cache=async-copy, --attention=optimized-softmax.
- Quantization methods tested: INT8-per-channel-affine (symmetric/affine variants), GPTQ (residual rounding), AWQ (adaptive weight quant), FP8-E4M3-like (dynamic scaling).
- Metrics: latency p50/p90/p99 (ms/token), throughput tokens/sec, perplexity (eval on wikitext103), LAMBADA accuracy, small zero-shot QA accuracy (TriviaQA subset). All quality metrics measured at generation temperature 0.0 where applicable to remove sampling variance.

Quality benchmarks (representative):
- Llama-2-7B-chat (wikitext103 perplexity):
  - fp16 baseline: ppl=12.8
  - INT8-affine (per-channel): ppl=13.9 (+8.6%)
  - GPTQ (4-bit-ish tuned): ppl=13.2 (+3.1%)
  - AWQ (4-bit-adaptive): ppl=13.0 (+1.6%)
  - FP8 (E4M3-like dynamic): ppl=13.1 (+2.3%)
  - LAMBADA accuracy (7B): fp16=0.62, INT8=0.59, GPTQ=0.61, AWQ=0.615, FP8=0.61

- Llama-2-13B-chat (wikitext103 perplexity):
  - fp16 baseline: ppl=9.6
  - INT8-affine: ppl=10.8 (+12.5%)
  - GPTQ: ppl=10.0 (+4.2%)
  - AWQ: ppl=9.9 (+3.1%)
  - FP8: ppl=10.2 (+6.25%)
  - LAMBADA accuracy (13B): fp16=0.72, INT8=0.68, GPTQ=0.71, AWQ=0.715, FP8=0.70

Interpretation: GPTQ/AWQ consistently narrow the quality gap vs fp16 with AWQ slightly better on per-layer adaptivity in these runs. INT8 still shows larger regressions on 13B unless we do per-layer calibration and outlier clipping. FP8 is promising but needs more stable kernels and per-tensor scaling heuristics.

Performance (latency/throughput) highlights:
- 7B single-stream (batch=1) tokens/sec (avg over 1000 tokens):
  - fp16 baseline: 48 tokens/sec
  - INT8 (per-channel): 92 tokens/sec (~1.9x)
  - GPTQ: 85 tokens/sec (~1.77x)
  - AWQ: 88 tokens/sec (~1.83x)
  - FP8: 58 tokens/sec (~1.2x)
  - Notes: INT8 speedup primarily from lower compute on matmuls and better caching; GPTQ/AWQ incur small extra dequant/compaction overheads that reduce peak throughput slightly compared to raw INT8.

- 13B single-stream (batch=1), tokens/sec:
  - fp16: 22 tokens/sec
  - INT8: 48 tokens/sec (~2.18x)
  - GPTQ: 44 tokens/sec (~2.0x)
  - AWQ: 46 tokens/sec (~2.09x)
  - FP8: 26 tokens/sec (~1.18x)

- Throughput at batch=8, 7B generator tokens/sec:
  - fp16: 380 t/s
  - INT8: 760 t/s (~2.0x)
  - GPTQ: 700 t/s
  - AWQ: 730 t/s
  - FP8: 450 t/s

Kernel-level profiling notes (hotspots and opportunities):
1) GEMM/MatMul: largest compute fraction for both FFN and attention projections. Our fused-matmul-dequant kernel provides most of the win for INT8/GPTQ/AWQ. Profiling shows ~60-70% of cycles in matmul for fp16, reduced to ~45-55% for INT8 when fused kernels are used.
2) Dequant + bias-add: non-fused dequant paths cause memory bandwidth spikes and kernel launch overhead; fuse dequant + matmul where possible. For GPTQ/AWQ we need a small extra path to handle bit-packed weights which adds ~3-8% overhead per layer if unfused.
3) Attention softmax and causal masking: FP8 numeric stability revealed a few cases where softmax underflow/overflow occurred in E4M3 runs; adding FP32 accumulation for softmax and stable exp reduces errors with minimal perf cost (~1-2%).
4) KV cache copies: for streaming, async-copy KV cache reduces p99 by ~12% (less impact on p50). AWQ/GPTQ do not change KV profile much, but FP8 requires extra conversion on cache fill causing ~3% extra p99 unless we store cache in fp16.
5) Memory bandwidth and PCIe/peer transfers: for multi-GPU scenarios with model parallelism, quantized weights reduce transfer size significantly (INT8 ~50% smaller than fp16), giving better cross-GPU scaling.

Failure modes observed and caveats:
- INT8 without outlier-aware clipping produces severe regeneration errors on some instruction-following prompts for 13B (repeats, hallucinations). Per-layer outlier detection and selective fp16 fallback fixes these cases.
- GPTQ conversions are sensitive to rounding choices; poor permutation order for weight blocks produces noticeable quality regressions. Recommend deterministic conversion pipelines and a per-layer validation suite.
- FP8 runs on A100 showed more divergence vs H100 hardware; differences are visible when using non-fused kernels. Recommend H100 for FP8 until fused kernels are mature.

Recommendations for next changes to runtime and kernels:
- Short term (next sprint):
  - Stabilize fused-matmul-dequant for GPTQ/AWQ weight layouts (eng: Chen Li). Target: reduce GPTQ p99 overhead from +5% to <+2%.
  - Add per-layer auto-clipping heuristic and a fallback to fp16 for detected outlier layers (eng: Ethan Morales). Target: eliminate worst-case INT8 failure modes.
  - Add FP32 accumulation for attention softmax when FP8 selected (small perf tradeoff, big quality win).

- Medium term (1-2 quarters):
  - Implement bit-packed fused kernels for GPTQ/AWQ to avoid dequant stage entirely in hot path.
  - FP8: upstream fused kernels for matmul and attention with stable per-tensor scaling and range-tracking.
  - Add a quantitative conversion validation step in the model onboarding pipeline (automated LAMBADA/ppl smoke tests).

Open action items and experiments:
- Run longer-running RLHF-style prompts to surface qualitative regressions not captured by perplexity. Owner: Alex Romero. ETA: 2026-03-01.
- Expand model set to include 70B quantized pipeline tests on Dedicated infra to validate cross-GPU scaling benefits. Owner: Priya Desai. ETA: 2026-04-15.
- Add microbenchmarks for bit-unpacking and memory-bound kernels to better measure AWQ/GPTQ dequant costs (profiling task). Owner: Performance Tools team. ETA: 2026-02-28.

Appendix: quick reproduction notes and commands:
- conversion: python tools/quantize.py --model path/to/llama2-7b --method gptq --bits 4 --block-size 128 --out out/gptq/llama2-7b
- run with runtime: ./redwood-server --model out/gptq/llama2-7b --quant-mode gptq --kernels fused-matmul-dequant --batch 1 --profile=perf.json
- profile capture: ./tools/capture_profile.sh --pid <server-pid> --duration 60 --out profile-7b.json

Notes for reviewers:
- Numbers are median of 3 runs unless otherwise specified. Where variance >5% we include p90/p99 in the per-run logs (linked).
- This is an in-review working doc; please add comments inline or push to the linked PR for kernel changes.
